articles.title: FSU running back signs with NFC North team
articles.summary: Roydell Williams was not selected during the 2026 NFL Draft but he will get a shot after signing with the Detroit Lions as the preseason rolls on.
articles.body:
Roydell Williams will have the opportunity to play for an NFL team.

The former FSU running back was not selected during the 2026 NFL Draft but has signed with the Detroit Lions as the preseason nears its conclusion. The team posted the info to their X page, although details of the contract were not disclosed.

Williams spent two seasons with the Seminoles, joining the team as a transfer from the Alabama Crimson Tide in 2024. At FSU, he played in 10 games and rushed for 99 yards and two touchdowns, but was injured for much of his time in Tallahassee. With the Crimson Tide, he totaled 1,165 rushing yards and scored 11 touchdowns.

He reunites with Alabama teammate Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit, who is their feature back. Detroit has been looking for depth at the running back position, and it's possible Williams shores it up.

The Detroit Lions went 9-8 last season under head coach Dan Campbell, missing the playoffs last season in the suddenly hyper-competitive NFC North. The Lions have the sixth-easiest strength of schedule in the league this season, so whether they can bounce back and return to the playoffs remains to be seen.

articles.title: Texans predicted to replace David Montgomery in 2027 ESPN mock draft with 24-TD Ole Miss RB
articles.summary: This would be a bold decision from the Texans after just trading for Montgomery.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans ' defense is one of, if not the best, units in the NFL. Even with a mediocre offense, this defense should carry the Texans to the playoffs.

But, that doesn't mean they shouldn't be looking to upgrade the offense. The tight end and wide receiver rooms aren't terrible, but they're in flux. The offensive line is shaky and C.J. Stroud might not be the franchise guy after bad end 2026.

The running back room is very strong, but ESPN's Jordan Reid is predicting they're going to replace David Montgomery or Woody Marks in the 2027 NFL Draft by taking 24-touchdown Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy.

Texans predicted to replace their starting RBs with Kewan Lacy

"20. Houston Texans . Kewan Lacy, RB, Ole Miss," Reid predicts. "The Texans have a deep roster, but they could use some reinforcements at running back."

Even though the Texans just traded for Montgomery this offseason, Reid is predicting they prepare to move on from the veteran RB, as he's turning 30 years old next season.

Marks has shown flashes, but Reid is still predicting the Texans land Lacy, the best running back in next year's draft class, in the first round of this ESPN mock draft.

Lacy ran the ball 306 times for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns for the Ole Miss Rebels last year. That's incredibly impressive, and something that any RB-needy team would love to add to their roster next year.

But first-round running backs cost a lot, and might not be worth it. Though in this mock draft scenario, using the 20th pick on Lacy wouldn't be a terrible overpay considering his talents.

If he has another huge season in 2026, then Lacy might not even make it down the board this far. The upside with Lacy is incredible, and the Texans could use a superstar on offense outside of Nico Collins .

Montgomery and Marks are good running backs, but landing someone as good as Lacy, with the hope that he turns into one of the best RBs in the NFL, is intriguing enough to spend a first-round pick on him.

articles.title: Stock Up: Which Cowboys are trending heading into preseason finale?
articles.summary: The depth at receiver and running back, plus Ajani Cornelius at right guard, have all raised their stock for the Cowboys' offense.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 34-13 ; their second convincing preseason victory. In both contests, the defense showed up and played extremely well, but this time the offense followed suit. Joe Milton getting the start and going off is the biggest reason. He threw for 179 yards and two touchdowns plus ran in another score.

Beyond his well documented and heavily discussed success, there are still other areas which were bolded question marks coming into the exhibition schedule. There was the battle between the receivers below the top three options, as well as the running back group beyond Javonte Williams .

With one preseason game left to go that will almost certainly see the majority of players expected to see regular-season action on the sidelines, here's whose stock is highest.

Ajani Cornelius moved from tackle over to guard and played almost 100 preseason snaps. His PFF overall grade is 87.3, and he hasn't allowed the quarterback to be touched, giving up only two pressures in 50 pass-blocking reps. This is incredibly important for a Cowboys team badly needing offensive line depth after losing multiple solid backups in free agency. The offensive line hasn't been a strong suit, with most believing T.J. Bass is the only reserve who could start if any of the starting five were injured. If Cornelius can be a backup offensive guard with a ton of college right tackle experience, it could reset the depth on the unit.

Another solid performance this Friday against the Saints , in what should be an extended look, could earn him a spot on the 53-man roster.

The running back room has a top-end starter in Williams, and the depth begins with the guy nobody seems to want, Malik Davis . He isn't flashy, but he doesn't have major holes in his game. He gets what's blocked for him on run plays, he can bring in a pass, his blocking is as good as Williams, and he plays special teams at a high level.

In the latest preseason game, he caught a touchdown pass, blocked in pass protection to set up a big play, and rushed for nearly 6 yards per attempt. Dallas has their main backup, and the change-of-pace option finally showed up in Arizona.

Jaydon Blue is who fans want as the backup, as he has an explosive element the Cowboys are currently missing from their rushing attack. Blue ran the ball 15 times for 75 yards and looked like an NFL rusher. He ran between the tackles and fell forward as he was being tackled. The guys likely to make the practice squad, Israel Abanikanda and Phil Mafah , both also had good moments against the Cardinals .

Mafah took his only carry for a 15-yard touchdown without great blocking to lead him, and Abanikanda had eight rushes for 49 yards. The whole room showed up well in the second preseason game, and Friday's contest could be a deciding factor in not just the 53-man roster, but also the practice squad.

Camden Brown began the year as possibly the last receiver on the depth chart. If he were only judged on this camp, Jonathan Mingo would probably be a lock for the roster. The two are battling it out for the fifth receiver spot, and the fact that it's them atop the heap is a shock to most.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling is a known vet who some thought could take Mingo's spot. Tyler Johnson and Denzel Mims are other veterans with production in NFL games, and Anthony Smith was a 2026 draft pick.

Brown shouldn't compete for the fifth receiving position, but he is because he has had an incredible camp. He has led the team in receiving yards both games, and his stat line of seven targets, five catches, 139 yards, and two touchdowns is impressive.

Mingo finally showing what made him a second-round pick, along with excellent special-teams play could have the edge. The teams play is a key to being the fifth receiver option, and a 53-yard, deep-ball touchdown reception have Mingo right in the mix. He is the second-highest-graded receiver in the preseason for Pro Football Focus with a grade of 90.5. The receiving battle for the fifth spot could force the Cowboys into keeping six receivers.

You can find Mike Crum on Twitter @cdpiglet or on YouTube at Across the Cowboys podcast

articles.title: SEC to issue harsh punishments for teams that add former pro athletes
articles.summary: The SEC is finalizing some harsh penalties for teams that violate its new professional players ban in the conference.
articles.body:
The SEC has settled on some harsh punishments for any member schools that sign a former professional player to its roster going forward, according to multiple reports on Wednesday, Aug. 26.

The conference unanimously passed ruling to ban former professional players from returning to college on Aug. 25, following a vote. Teams in violation of the SEC's new rules against former professional athletes returning to college will receive the following penalties:

50% of season suspension for head coaches

50% of that sport's annual operating budget

SEC voting privileges revoked on some matters

It's a gloves-off approach for the SEC, which is taking a hard stance against players entering the professional ranks before attempting to change their minds and return to college. The ruling comes amid multiple former NFL signees attempting returns to college football after gaining an extra season of eligibility, thanks to a temporary restraining order ruling in Louisiana state court this offseason.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference ," the SEC's statement read on Aug. 25. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition.

"Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes."

The Big Ten was the first Power Four conference to agree on rules against the situation, which has gained attention after LSU has added former Ole Miss standouts Dae'Quan Wright and Xzavian Harris, who both signed NFL contracts as undrafted free agents. The two players played under head coach Lane Kiffin for the Rebels, and gained extra seasons due to the court decision, which had a basis due to the NCAA's new 5-for-5 eligibility ruling.

It's unclear how the ruling impacts Wright and Harris' eligibility moving forward.

Kiffin told Pat McAfee on Aug. 25 that he doesn't agree with professional players returning to the college ranks, but that Wright and Harris' situation was different based on 5-for-5.

"There's a lot of parts of this I don't like," Kiffin said. "I don't think professionals should come back to college sports and college football. But in this instance, these are not players who have gone on to play seasons professionally or randomly filed an injunction. This is part of a specific class that was ruled wrong by the NCAA that was supposed to be 5-for-5."

SEC punishments for signing former professional player

The SEC's new punishments bar any team from signing former professional players from any level, whether it's the NBA's G-League, the NFL or the WNBA, for example.

articles.title: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst says team is 'prepared' for possible Josh Jacobs suspension
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs has yet to face punishment from the NFL after a May arrest.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested in May and booked on five charges following an alleged domestic-violence situation. At the time, the NFL said it was aware of the situation, but has yet to issue any sort of punishment against the running back.

But the Packers know a suspension is a possibility, and are "prepared" for that scenario, team general manager Brian Gutekunst told reporters Wednesday.

When asked about Jacobs' situation, Gutekunst took it as an opportunity to say the team feels good about its depth at running back.

With just two weeks to go until the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, the league needs to act quickly if Jacobs is going to miss time early in the regular season. It's unclear whether that will happen.

The NFL typically likes to let the legal process play out before issuing suspensions to players. That's the track the league took with New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara following a 2022 arrest. With Kamara's legal situation still ongoing at the start of the 2022 NFL season, the league waited to issue discipline to the running back. Kamara was allowed to play and took part in 15 games before the league issued a three-game suspension to Kamara ahead of the 2023 NFL season.

But the league might feel compelled to act early in this instance. During an August radio appearance in Milwaukee, ESPN's Adam Schefter said the league could look to be proactive in Jacobs' case. While Schefter hedged with his reporting, he ultimately said he would "not be surprised if there is discipline by the time the season starts."

When on the field, Jacobs has proven to be an excellent, durable runner. In two seasons with the Packers, he's rushed for 2,258 yards and 28 touchdowns.

If Jacobs is suspended in 2026, his workload would fall to some combination of Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd . Since being drafted in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, Lloyd has played in just one game due to injuries.

Brooks, meanwhile, has spent the last two years in Green Bay . He's received 63 rushing attempts over that period, gaining 289 yards and scoring one touchdown.
